headline.one_sentence: PCQM-1M has enough crossed structure for partial response reuse, but additive SHARED composition and the overall LOCAL context rule stay below their pre-registered practical screens; ZINC is structurally acyclic and cannot test crossed response reuse.

answers.q: Q1. Is there enough crossed structural support for transfer, and which dataset qualifies?
answers.answer: PCQM-1M qualifies: 4,824,824 cells, 3,166,455 C contexts, 987,596 molecules; primary 64-S graph has 3 components (largest 3,010,213), 2-core 419,353, cycle rank 777,293; 1,602 supported pairs and 96,991 disjoint evaluation pair observations. ZINC does not: 0 supported pairs, primary graph 2-core 6 and cycle rank 1, 0 evaluation pair observations.

answers.q: Q2. Does a discovery response reuse on evaluation contexts (P1)?
answers.answer: PCQM: PARTIAL_RESPONSE_REUSE. Context-equal PAIR MAE 0.23657 vs ZERO 0.26554 (gain 10.91%, paired 95% CI for ZERO-PAIR [0.02725, 0.03071]); sign accuracy 0.647. Pair-equal gives MAE 0.26215 vs 0.29750 (gain 11.88%). ZINC: INSUFFICIENT_CROSSED_SUPPORT.

answers.q: Q3. Are stable functional-equivalence candidates useful, and how much do they cover (P1)?
answers.answer: Only narrowly. At tau=0.10 there are 3 frozen candidates, covering 0.19% of supported pairs; 77.8% of their 415 evaluation observations stay within tau. At tau=0.20 there are 151 candidates (9.43% coverage) and 83.1% stay within tau. Stable equivalence is real but sparse; it is not a broad replacement dictionary.

answers.q: Q4. Does additive SHARED composition support unobserved replacement (P2)?
answers.answer: No at the pre-registered 15% screen. Natural unobserved pairs: 0. Controlled masking: 16 applicable pairs, 18,584 evaluation observations. SHARED MAE 0.16924 vs ZERO 0.17083: gain 0.93% (CI [0.00002, 0.00321]); PAIR-FULL reference 0.16209, so SHARED remains 0.00715 worse. Macro pair-equal gain 2.31%. Verdict COMPOSITION_SCREEN_ONLY. Supplementary condition corrections fitted after masking give MAE 0.15423 (gain 8.87% vs SHARED), showing that context rules, not the global additive term, carry most of the signal.

answers.q: Q5. Does a LOCAL context rule beat SHARED and a matched NULL (P3)?
answers.answer: Directionally yes, but below the overall 10% screen: 114 supported q groups, correction coverage 99.00%; LOCAL MAE 0.24881 vs SHARED 0.27145 (gain 8.34%, CI [0.02105, 0.02425]) and vs LOCAL_NULL 0.27319 (gain 8.93%). On the discovery-frozen high-non-additivity quartile (442 pairs, 12223 observations), LOCAL gain is 10.76% (CI [0.04476, 0.05457]). Verdict CONTEXT_RULE_SCREEN_ONLY: real q signal, but the pre-registered overall 10% bar is not met.

answers.q: Q6. Does ZINC reproduce or contradict the PCQM conclusions?
answers.answer: ZINC is a structural negative control, not a contradiction: its primary bipartite graph is almost a forest (44 components, largest 20,194, 2-core 6, cycle rank 1), so 0 pairs have both >=10 discovery and >=5 evaluation contexts, and there are 0 evaluation pair observations. P1/P2/P3 are labelled INSUFFICIENT_CROSSED_SUPPORT or CONTEXT_SUPPORT_INSUFFICIENT; no label-based claim is made.

answers.q: Q7. Does the official PCQM Valid split confirm transfer without touching Test labels?
answers.answer: Yes, descriptively. On 36,952 Valid pair observations with a frozen discovery median, PAIR MAE 0.29795 vs ZERO 0.34791 (skill 14.36%, sign 0.674); unseen exact contexts: skill 5.59%; seen exact contexts: skill 15.53%. 7,356 cells from 1,819 Valid molecules duplicate Train graphs and were excluded. Official Test labels were never read; Test was not built.

answers.q: Q8. Are identity, reconstruction, labels, splits, and controls clean enough to trust the verdicts?
answers.answer: Yes within the recorded limits. PCQM graph reassembly: 57,873 sampled cuts, 0 graph failures; stereo exactness 91.1% (5,128 mismatches, reported separately). ZINC: 20,000 cuts, 0 exact-certificate failures. 1,000/1,000 sampled PCQM SMILES and labels match the raw CSV; all 1M rows are unique and inside official Train; discovery/evaluation molecule overlap is 0; primary evaluation contexts share no molecule. 10,557 duplicate PCQM molecules carry labels differing by up to 4.94 eV; they are one identity but the label conflict is a known noise source. All five FP64 controls pass. All checks pass.

limitations: PCQM-1M is a prefix of official Train, not the full 3.38M Train rows; support is ample, so no full-Train expansion was justified.
Identity is graph-level; 8.9% of sampled PCQM stereo reassemblies differ and are tracked separately.
Duplicate whole graphs can carry conflicting labels (max 4.94 eV); they share one molecule identity but add label noise.
P2/P3 are observational screens with context-level bootstrap; they are not causal or population theorems.
The 64-S vocabulary, tau, ridge lambda, and 10%/15% screens are fixed practical choices chosen before labels.
ZINC is a structural negative control: almost no cycles means the crossed pair design is unavailable.
deviations: ZINC exact-certificate reassembly was capped at 20,000 cuts for runtime; all 66,494 cut invariants and all PCQM graph reassembly checks passed.
PCQM functional-equivalence candidate rows with zero evaluation observations are reported but excluded from fraction-within-tau aggregates.
P2 condition corrections after masking are supplementary to the pre-registered SHARED judgment; the P2 verdict remains based on SHARED.

The P1 scaffold-cluster bootstrap and the P2 post-masking LOCAL scoring were executed as protocol-specified secondary analyses after the primary P1/P2 runs; no threshold, vocabulary, split, or primary verdict was changed.
